description: Verifies the electrovacuum and cosmological metrics: Reissner-Nordstrom and Kerr-Newman horizons and regimes, Kerr-Newman reduction to Kerr, geometric invariants of Reissner-Nordstrom, Kerr-Newman, Schwarzschild-de Sitter and Kerr-de Sitter, and the FLRW scale factor, redshift and metric inversion.

checks.label: Q / M = 0.6 is sub-extremal
the outer horizon equals M + sqrt(M^2 - Q^2) = 1.8
the inner horizon equals M - sqrt(M^2 - Q^2) = 0.2
Q = M is extremal
the extremal outer horizon sits at M
the extremal inner horizon sits at M
Q > M is hyper-extremal
the uncharged photon sphere radius equals 3 M
Reissner-Nordstrom: the inverse metric times the metric reproduces the identity
Reissner-Nordstrom: the metric tensor is symmetric relative to its largest component
Reissner-Nordstrom: the metric determinant is negative, which gives a Lorentzian signature
Reissner-Nordstrom: the analytic connection is symmetric in its lower indices
Reissner-Nordstrom: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
a^2 + Q^2 < M^2 is sub-extremal
the outer horizon equals M + sqrt(M^2 - a^2 - Q^2)
the uncharged Kerr-Newman metric inverts to the identity
Kerr-Newman: the inverse metric times the metric reproduces the identity
Kerr-Newman: the metric tensor is symmetric relative to its largest component
Kerr-Newman: the metric determinant is negative, which gives a Lorentzian signature
Kerr-Newman: the analytic connection is symmetric in its lower indices
Kerr-Newman: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
Schwarzschild-de Sitter: the inverse metric times the metric reproduces the identity
Schwarzschild-de Sitter: the metric tensor is symmetric relative to its largest component
Schwarzschild-de Sitter: the metric determinant is negative, which gives a Lorentzian signature
Schwarzschild-de Sitter: the analytic connection is symmetric in its lower indices
Schwarzschild-de Sitter: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
Kerr-de Sitter: the inverse metric times the metric reproduces the identity
Kerr-de Sitter: the metric tensor is symmetric relative to its largest component
Kerr-de Sitter: the metric determinant is negative, which gives a Lorentzian signature
Kerr-de Sitter: the analytic connection is symmetric in its lower indices
Kerr-de Sitter: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
the matter-dominated scale factor equals 1 at t0
the matter-dominated scale factor grows as t^(2/3), giving 4 at t = 8
the cosmological redshift between t = 1 and t = 8 equals 3
the FLRW inverse metric reproduces the identity
